title: Score narration fidelity on the script
statement: Score a narration's fidelity to its source on the script, not a recogniser's transcript, whose errors count as changes, and use recognition only to confirm the audio reads it.
example: Scored on a recogniser's transcript, a film whose script matched its source word for word came out at 98.4%.
detail: A comparison of three opening films found that all three read the same 434-word script verbatim, while the recogniser heard 432, 429 and 427 of 436 normalised words, its misses being numerals, homophones and name spellings plus a few words that may be misread or mispronounced (`g9/library/text/L88a690.txt`, lines 27-28). Scored on the recogniser's output instead of its script, one film came out at 98.4%, purely from recogniser errors such as "bruined" counted as script changes (lines 52-54; `g9/library/text/L4fa28c.txt`, line 32). Since then fidelity is measured on each film's script, with the recogniser used only to confirm the audio reads it.
against: A recogniser's misses can still hide real misreadings, so each still needs a listen: "plus a few words that may be misread or mispronounced" (`g9/library/text/L88a690.txt`, line 28).
